text:
maria: Hey team, seeing a perf regression in nightly for the serving runtime.
The symptom: a 2-3x tail latency spike on a small subset of requests that hit KV cache misses and then seem to trigger a different kernel path (we suspect an int8 fallback).
Anyone have a recommended nsys capture command and sampling/capture strategy so I can get a clean kernel timeline and the OS runtime markers?

ashok: For this class of problem I usually do short bracketed captures around the single offending request. Warm up the model 2-3x, then bracket the NVTX range around a single request to keep capture sizes small.
Example I run locally:
```
# warmup loop outside capture
nsys profile -o kvreg-1 --trace=cuda,nvtx,osrt --sample-interval=200us --capture-range=nvtx --capture-range-start=main:start --capture-range-end=main:end --duration=30 python serve_trace.py
```
Notes: --trace=cuda,nvtx,osrt gives you kernels + NVTX + OS runtime threads; sample-interval 200us balances fidelity and file size. Use --capture-range to avoid huge traces.

kelly: Also try a bracketed run with `--sample=none` to get precise kernel timings (non-sampled) if you have room for bigger files. Once you identify the hot kernel, switch back to sampled short runs for iteration.

sam: If you suspect backend kernel selection flip (e.g., fp16->int8 path), add env dumps around the capture. For PyTorch/TorchScript layers we add `NVPROF_REPLAY_MODE=1`? Not ideal — instead annotate code with NVTX before the op that touches KV cache and right after eviction so you can clearly see which kernels are associated with KV hits vs misses.
Example NVTX snippet: `nvtxRangePushA("kv-lookup-start")` / `nvtxRangePop()` around the request handler.

maria: Good call. Any tips on sampling duration and # of samples? CI currently grabs 5s traces which are noisy and miss the long tail.

ashok: Increase to 20-60s for a bracketed run if you can (but use capture-range!). For sampling: shorter intervals like 100-200us pick up short kernels; 1ms can miss microbursts. I usually iterate: 200us to explore, then 100us once narrowed.
Also: run a handful of captures (3-5) to see reproducibility — the tail might be correlated with eviction timing and GPU memory fragmentation.

kelly: On the GUI, look at the GPU kernel list sorted by "GPU Time (ms)" not just count. If you see a single kernel suddenly dominating in the tail runs, check its grid/block params in the details pane — that tells you which implementation variant ran. That helps validate kernel-selection changes.

sam: Another quick check: enable `--export=cupti`? (or the nsys equivalent) so you can run `nsys stats` on the qdrep and get aggregate metrics. Also save the .qdrep files and upload to the perf bucket for us to inspect.

ci-bot: Reminder: uploads >200MB will get pruned in CI. Consider `--sample-interval=500us` for CI-friendly captures or trim with capture-range.

maria: Thanks — I'll run bracketed 3x captures with NVTX around the handler, 200us sampling, 45s duration, and attach .qdrep. I'll also annotate eviction points. Will report back with one qdrep link. :thumbsup:

ashok: If you get a candidate kernel, ping me and I'll pull it into the kernel list mapping script to map names to our kernel-impl IDs. Also note whether the kernel shows `__torch_` / `cutlass` / `mha` prefixes — that hints at backend selection.

kelly: One last tip: on the timeline check the OS runtime (osrt) thread for long gaps before the kernel launch — that often indicates CPU-side scheduling or queueing which can make it look like a kernel issue.

maria: Great. Will run and attach. Thanks!
